items.title: Professor’s Death Leaves Behind Hard Questions for Cambridge on Race and Hiring
items.summary: Jason Arday, the school’s youngest Black professor, was found dead on Friday. The school ignored a series of warnings about his life story and his work.

items.title: The Iranian YouTube Show Posing Questions Few Dare Ask
items.summary: Azad, a popular online debate program, has tackled topics that push the limits of Iran’s authoritarian system. Some question how it has remained on air.

items.title: Canadian Petition to Expel U.S. Ambassador Pete Hoekstra Takes Off
items.summary: Mr. Hoekstra has been President Trump’s faithful messenger in Canada amid a historic low in relations. More than 160,000 Canadians want him gone.

items.title: Wary of Trump, Europe Seeks Role in Eventual Russia-Ukraine Talks
items.summary: French, German and British diplomats are working on a format for future negotiations — even if Russia has shown little interest.

items.title: Israeli Strikes in Lebanon Kill 11, Health Officials Say
items.summary: The Lebanese health ministry said several children were killed in a strike overnight, one of the deadliest attacks in months. Israel’s military said it was targeting Hezbollah infrastructure.

items.title: At Least 47 Dead as 7.7-Magnitude Earthquake Rocks Indonesia
items.summary: The temblor was one of the strongest the area had experienced in decades, an official said.

items.title: Entrenched, Embattled and Defiant, the Taliban Celebrate 5 Years in Power
items.summary: The Taliban have Afghanistan in a chokehold that spares no one. But threats are starting to crack their veneer of stability and control.

items.title: Heat Deaths in a ‘Cold’ Country Are a Warning to the Rest of Europe
items.summary: A June heat wave in Belgium and neighboring countries exposed a lethal lack of readiness. That’s a risk as another wave hits Europe.

items.title: Russia Campaigned to Derail Moldova’s Pro-Western Government
items.summary: In Moldova, Moscow paid Orthodox priests, conducted a vote-buying scheme and set up training camps on election interference — all in an effort to derail the Western-leaning government.

items.title: Heat Is Hammering Europe, Again. Here’s What That Looks Like.
items.summary: Extreme temperatures and repeated wildfires are pushing infrastructure to the limit and testing the continent’s resolve.

items.title: The Cutthroat Wearables Battle Is About More Than Tracking Your Fitness
items.summary: Google, Apple, Samsung and upstarts like Oura are racing to integrate data from their wearable devices into the health care system.

items.title: Sports Team Sale Prices Keep Hitting New Highs

items.title: Worker Pay Isn’t Keeping Up With Inflation Once Again
items.summary: When prices spiked in 2021-22, wages failed to keep up for many workers, new research shows. Now the pattern is repeating.

items.title: How to Protect Your Home While You’re on Vacation
items.summary: Store food in sealed containers and fix any leaking faucets or pipes, experts told our columnist, who had her own nightmare upon returning home.

items.title: How Cyclospora Evaded the U.S. Food Safety System to Sicken Thousands
items.summary: The Trump administration delayed a rule last year that could have sped up the effort to pinpoint the source of the contamination. Critics charge that food safety oversight has eroded overall.

items.title: FDA Classifies Egg Recall as Class I for Highest Health Risk
items.summary: Nearly 20 million eggs were recalled in July over salmonella concerns. The new classification signals a “reasonable probability” of “serious adverse health consequences or death.”

items.title: Hiroshi Okuda, Disrupter Who Revived Toyota in the 1990s, Dies at 93
items.summary: As the car company’s president, he made decisions quickly and shook things up, expanding overseas manufacturing and introducing the Prius, a milestone in automotive history.

items.title: Lawsuit Accuses Selena Gomez of Defrauding Investors in Mental Health Site
items.summary: The actor, singer and beauty mogul founded Wondermind, a mental health platform, with her mother. Investors put in more than $1 million in the venture, which “quietly collapsed,” the suit said.

items.title: Google Turns On Gemini A.I. for Students Using Its Classroom App
items.summary: Google enabled A.I. features for K-12 schools that have allowed student access to Gemini. Until this week, Google automatically enabled Gemini in Classroom only for students 18 or older.

items.title: Outrage at UnitedHealth and Other Insurers Persists After Brian Thompson Killing
